gloss: total stranger; unknown person; someone never met before

definitions.gloss: total stranger; unknown person; someone one has never seen or met
definitions.explanation: A person one has never seen ({見|み}ず) and does not know ({知|し}らず). Emphasizes the complete lack of prior acquaintance.

examples.japanese: {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{話|はな}しかけられた→話しかける：03134_hanashikakeru⟧。
examples.english: I was spoken to by a total stranger.

examples.japanese: {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{迷|まよ}って→迷う：02426_mayou⟧しまった。
examples.english: I got lost in an unfamiliar place.

examples.japanese: {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{簡単|かんたん}→簡単：00713_kantan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{信用|しんよう}して→信用する：25371_shinyousuru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't easily trust people you don't know.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧ず (not having seen - negative form of ⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧)
+ ⟦{知|し}ら→知る：00458_shiru⟧ず (not knowing - negative form of ⟦{知|し}る→知る：00458_shiru⟧)

The classical negative suffix ず creates a formal/literary compound.
- {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ + noun (as no-adjective)
- {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ - a person one doesn't know
- {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧ - unfamiliar land

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ - total stranger (person)
- {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧/⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧ - unfamiliar place
- {見|み}ず{知|し}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{他人|たにん}→他人：01459_tanin⟧ - complete stranger

USAGE:
Can modify both people and places, unlike ⟦{赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}→赤の他人：07455_akanotanin⟧ which only refers to people.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}→赤の他人：07455_akanotanin⟧ - complete stranger (emphasizes no relationship)
- ⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ - unknown person (simpler)
- {行|ゆ}きずり - passerby, chance encounter
- ⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦{会|あ}う→会う：00482_au⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ - person meeting for the first time

REGISTER:
Slightly literary due to classical negative form ず. Natural in both spoken and written Japanese.
